history.period: Groundbreaking 1977; opened to the public 22 February 1988 (consecrated 22 February 1985 per one source - verify)
history.summary: This is the famous Birla Mandir of Jaipur, also called the Lakshmi Narayan Temple - dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Vishnu (Narayan), with images of other Hindu gods and goddesses and selections from the Gita and Upanishads inside. Built by the B.M. Birla Foundation (construction 1977 under Ramanauj Das and Ghanshyam Birla), it is constructed entirely of white marble and stands at the base of Moti Doongari hill in the Tilak Nagar neighbourhood of Jaipur. Tradition states the Maharaja of Jaipur sold the Birla family the land for one rupee. The temple has a sanctum, tower, main hall and entrance, with three towers said to reference the three main faiths of India; its outer walls carry figures of diverse religious and philosophical figures (Christ, the Virgin Mary, St Peter, Buddha, Confucius, Zarathustra, Socrates). Statues of founders Rukmani Devi Birla and Braj Mohan Birla stand outdoors in namaskara. CONFLICT NOTE: sources differ on whether 22 February 1985 was the consecration and 22 February 1988 the public opening; confirm before citing. CSV town and state (Jaipur, Rajasthan) are correct; no correction needed.

name: Birla Mandir
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan and the 'Pink City', is a major tourist and pilgrimage hub. Birla Mandir stands in Tilak Nagar at the base of Moti Doongari hill (site of the Moti Doongri fort and the famous Moti Doongri Ganesh temple opposite), on Jawahar Lal Nehru Marg, south of the walled city.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 10-12 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, about 4-5 km away (verify).
travel.road: On Jawahar Lal Nehru Marg in Tilak Nagar, Jaipur; easily reached by taxi, auto-rickshaw or local bus within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Diwali and Janmashtami for festive visits. Evening visits are popular as the marble temple is lit up at night.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 8:00 AM to 12:00 noon and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily by most travel guides - verify before visiting. No entry fee reported.
